prompt.brief: Design a real-time personalized recommendation service that ingests behavior events, combines fresh features with offline models, and returns diverse candidates within a tight latency budget.
successSignals: Define event collection, online feature freshness, candidate retrieval, ranking, filtering, exploration, diversity, and explanation contracts.
Combine collaborative, content-based, popular, and contextual candidates while preventing stale, unsafe, duplicate, or already-consumed items.
Keep the serving path bounded and cacheable; update features asynchronously and make event ingestion and model rollout idempotent.
Explain cold start, feedback loops, experimentation, privacy, fallback recommendations, observability, and model/index recovery.

functional: Ingest impressions, clicks, views, purchases, skips, and dislikes with deduplication and consent-aware retention.
Retrieve and rank personalized candidates with configurable filters, diversity, explanations, model/version metadata, and freshness.
Support anonymous and new-user recommendations, experimentation, user deletion/export, model rollback, and graceful fallback when features are missing.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 recommendation latency under 50ms for warm users and keep online-feature freshness under one minute.
Scale to millions of requests per minute without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous candidate work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: Millions of recommendation requests per minute and billions of catalog items/events
Partition online features and user caches by user; shard ANN/item indexes and precompute broad candidate pools.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Real-time personalized recommendation service commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Real-time personalized recommendation service writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Real-time personalized recommendation service version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Real-time personalized recommendation service by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Real-time personalized recommendation service work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Real-time personalized recommendation service projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Real-time personalized recommendation service projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Real-time personalized recommendation service records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Real-time personalized recommendation service latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
